reviews.title: Fabulous App!
reviews.text:
Thank you so much for creating this application.  I use it every day.  UPDATE:

After using this app for years, I have thought of a feature that would enhance this app.  For example I use this app primarily to monitor and take my medications on a strict schedule.  One of my timers is managing my pain medications, for example 8 hour Tylenol.  So I set a timer for 8 hours.  Whether or not I actually reset it or not. It would be beneficial if I could see how many times I actually reset it in a given time frame, for example a weekly or even a month’s time.   If there was a feature that automatically tallied my resets, I could show my doctor how many times I was taking the Tylenol.  My liver function tests might be influenced by how often I’m taking Tylenol.  I am unable to take any other pain meds based on my kidney disease so Tylenol is all I can take.  Please consider adding a feature like this.  I would gladly purchase a feature like this.  

I tried to message someone but can only put this request under the ‘reviews’ 
2nd update: I found the “History” feature which shows me daily the times I used the timer, but it would be nice to have a tally of the number of times I used the timer, by the month, 6 months and 1 year. 

Previous older review:

I have to take medicine every 8 hours, and the ease of using this app makes this the best ‘timer/countdown’ application ever!  
Why?:
1.  The application stay conveniently on the forefront of any application running, hiding on the side of the screen, ready to show itself with a slight swipe of the finger.
2.  The ease of setting up multiple timers/clocks and arranging them how you want them to be. 
3. The notifications of the end of a count down is unobtrusive and is no naggy like some alarms are. 
4. You can set up what side you would like the app to hide. 
5.  To start a timer or countdown, you just quickly tap on the circle with the timer in it. (Note:  this will only work like this if you do NOT have the set up menu bar showing at the top of the application.  It took me awhile to realize this.)
6. You can have multiple clocks showing from different time zones, eliminating my use of my iPads world clock app.  Which to me is very convenient.

My only con, is that the original instructions, once shown when first downloading are not found after you have used the app for the first time.  This was an annoyance as I could not figure out how to start the timers with a slight tap. See my note on #5 above.  

I would highly recommend anyone to get and use this app!

reviews.title: Great for cooking!
reviews.text:
Among many things this app is great for, it shines for cooking. Timers use live activities to keep the timer on the Lock Screen. You can also share pages of timers across the web, so others can track the time left on their devices. Glad to have multitimer in the toolkit for cooking as well as for workouts. 

The app has the option to configure timers as system alarms which solves the problem of third party timer apps being at the mercy of the phone’s silent/do not disturb status. I also recommend using the Shortcuts app to set a focus mode when opening MultiTimer, and configure the shortcut to 1) set the phone to silent mode off, 2) optionally set a specific lock screen with widgets optimized for timer-ing, and change the camera button (lower right) to a silent mode button (this displays a status indicator of silent mode that also works a one touch toggle for silent mode off/on).

I hope they add some streamlined view of currently active timers to make things a bit clearer to reduce the clutter when needed. I’ve been using the app for a decade, and I have requested as much, but the developers unfortunately do not see the value in an active timers dashboard.

reviews.title: MultiTimer with MultiBenefits
reviews.text:
**Always reliable and does exactly what I need**

This timer app has great feature with the ability to create groups of timers, arranged in different ways based on how you use them, and lots of types of timers (stopwatch, count down, count up, etc). Once created the timers can be quickly accessed and started using either the phone or Apple Watch, which is a welcome change compared to the built-in Apple timer. I bought the pro version and have been happy with my purchase. The only additional feature I would like is to be able to set up custom sounds and alarms. With that added feature this app would be perfect!

p.s. I love that you can export your created timers from one device and import them into another.

reviews.title: Change broke timer

Originally the sounds were at the beginning of the interval but when during a change to the software they moved the sound to the end of the step.  I spent the extra money so I could export my timers to other accounts which I also spent the extra money for - but now the time no longer works.  Additionally another inconvenience in this software is when you export and import a time to another account the voice recordings don’t follow.

reviews.title: Nice Offline Tracker
reviews.text:
MultiTimer is one of the most useful productivity apps I have ever used. The interface is clean, simple, intuitive, and powerful, making it easy to manage multiple timers simultaneously without confusion.

What I appreciate most is the flexibility of the app. Whether I need timers for work, studying, workouts, cooking, or daily routines, MultiTimer handles everything reliably and efficiently. The ability to organize timers into boards and customize them for different purposes makes it stand out from other timer applications.

The app is stable, well-designed, and clearly developed with attention to user experience. I have tried many timer apps over the years, but MultiTimer is the one that has remained on my device because it simply works and helps me stay organized.

reviews.title: Has a Fatal Flaw
reviews.text:
I think this is a wonderful app. Its purpose is straightforward to understand. If you have ADHD, a collection of pre-set timers that you can use to alert yourself to the status of ongoing timed tasks, is likely very important and useful to you. I use the app, for example, every laundry day to alert myself of the end of my washer and dryer cycles. 

But speaking as an iPhone user, there’s a big flaw with the app, and it’s sort of not its fault. Unlike the default IOS clock app, your timers won’t make any sound when they go off in silent mode. They also don’t go off continuously until you notice. Like any app notification, they ding for a few seconds and don’t come up again. 

Now, I get what you might say, “Well, just keep your phone on you with the volume high” and I’ll remind you that I use this app because of ADHD. It’s to be expected that I forgot I had timers set, that I turned my volume down low, that I took my phone off my person, etc. The irony of this app, is that in order for it to work, you have to be very alert to it working in the background, and keep checking it over and over, in case you missed an alert.

reviews.title: Year unit
reviews.text: Adding a year unit is extremely important to me. Its absence is actually the main reason I couldn’t continue using or subscribing to this app. It doesn’t make sense that some events show durations of more than 2,000 days, and then I have to manually calculate how many years and days that equals. A simple year display option would make long-term tracking far more practical and user-friendly.
